repo.name: Patchwork
repo.description: Personal patchwork builds of ScreenTime, RecurringExpenseTracker, Fcitx5 for Android and BasicSync.

application.name: BasicSync
application.desc:
A simple app for running Syncthing on Android.
The app is intentionally kept very basic so that the project is easy to maintain and keep updated. BasicSync only controls when Syncthing runs. The actual configuration is done through Syncthing's own web UI.
This patchwork build adds a navigation sidebar with the common pages (syncing, conflict management, settings, network conditions and the sync schedule) and a conflict management page where sync conflicts can be resolved manually by keeping the original file or by replacing it with the conflict version.
application.author: Andrew Gunnerson

application.name: Fcitx5 for Android
application.summary: Fcitx5 input method framework and engines, with Rime sync fixes
application.desc:
Fcitx5 for Android is the Android port of the Fcitx5 input method framework. It ships Pinyin (with Shuangpin support), Wubi and table-based input methods and can be extended with plugins such as Rime, Anthy, Hangul, Chewing, UniKey, Sayura, Thai and Jyutping.
This patchwork build starts from upstream 0.1.3 and adds: - the "All files access" (MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) permission, so librime can write its sync_dir on shared storage (for example Download/Rime-Sync); - a built-in Rime/Fcitx5 configuration file manager and UTF-8 editor; - cleanup of stale .temp.userdb files at startup, avoiding LOCK conflicts during sync; - a horizontal back arrow in the file manager.
Note: the package name matches the official app but the signing key differs, so the official version must be uninstalled before installing this build.
Fcitx5 for Android is free software under the LGPL-2.1; the corresponding source is the upstream repository plus the patch queue in this repository.
application.author: Fcitx5 for Android Contributors

application.name: Gadgetbridge
application.summary: Use your Bluetooth gadgets without the vendor's app, with a Compose UI
application.desc:
Gadgetbridge lets you use Bluetooth wearables and other gadgets without the vendor's closed-source application, without an account and without sending your data anywhere.
This patchwork build starts from upstream and adds: - a Jetpack Compose + Material 3 Expressive user interface: the settings tree, the first-run guide, the About page and the sleep score sheet are Compose, and the remaining screens inherit the larger Expressive shapes; - an age-based sleep score estimated from the recorded sleep stages when the device does not report one, with a breakdown sheet behind the score ring; - a backup that runs every time the app is opened, with its own settings page, a retention period and a folder the user can change; - a database export that writes to a temporary file, validates it and only then replaces the target, so a failed run cannot truncate the previous backup; - a single, complete music snapshot for Xiaomi devices, so the watch no longer shows a new title with an old playback state; - a time re-sync after every (re)connection.
Note: the package name matches the official app but the signing key differs, so the official version must be uninstalled before installing this build, which also means the recorded data does not carry over.
Gadgetbridge is free software under the AGPL-3.0; the corresponding source is the upstream repository plus the patch queue in this repository.
application.author: Gadgetbridge contributors

application.name: Recurring Expense Tracker
application.summary: Keep track of your monthly spending
application.desc:
A Material You recurring expense tracker, allowing you to keep track of your monthly spending.
As the name suggests, this app focuses on recurring expenses like rent, insurance, subscriptions, and other regular payments. Built with Kotlin Multiplatform and Material You design principles, it provides a simple yet powerful way to track and visualize your recurring financial commitments. The app is designed to be intuitive and straightforward, helping you understand exactly where your money goes each month. My idea is to add new features iteratively, and I'm happy for any contribution. Feel free to make feature requests or report bugs if you find any.
application.author: DennisBauer

application.name: Screen Time
application.summary: Easily track the time you spend on your device and apps.
application.desc:
Screen Time is a simple app that lets you easily track the time you spend on your device and apps.
Features:
- Displays total screen time for your device over the past week or for a chosen day. - Comparative graph showing screen time across different days of the week. - Comparative graph displaying screen time for each hour of the day. - Ability to view screen time and comparative graphs for each individual app. - Comparative list of screen time for each app, sorted from the most used to the least used during the chosen period. - Simple and modern interface. - Home screen widget. - No ads. - No data collection (internet permissions disabled). - Open source. - Developed in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose and Material 3.
The source code is available here: https://gitlab.com/Atharok/ScreenTime
application.author: Atharok

application.name: 百度网盘 Go
application.summary: Community patchwork build of the Baidu Netdisk client, with automatic encrypted backup.
application.desc:
The BaiduNetGo Android client of the community patchwork build of pengstem's Baidu Netdisk (百度网盘 Go) — a Material 3 Expressive app that pairs with the pure-Go desktop client published on the same repository.
Features:
- Sign in by scanning a QR code (or paste Cookie / BDUSS+STOKEN). - Browse the netdisk with list/grid views, sorting, search and file details. - Folder backup: pick local folders (SAF) and mirror them into a netdisk folder incrementally on a schedule (manual / 15 min / 1 h / 6 h / 24 h) in the background with WorkManager, or immediately with live progress. - Album backup: pick MediaStore albums and back their photos and videos up. - Encrypted backup: OpenPGP symmetric encryption turns every uploaded file into a .gpg that `gpg -d` opens on any computer — the same format the desktop client writes, so files from both devices restore alike. - Transfers with progress, speed and cancel. - Account and quota info, upload concurrency, Wi-Fi-only mode and themes.
Built from upstream plus the patch queue in this repository; the desktop half is released separately (it is not an F-Droid package).
application.author: pengstem
